about: Second pass (2026-10-08) for the 221 runnable models with a thin score (<3 counted results) listed in thin-runnable-2.json. Candidate rows only; data/*.json not edited. Merge results via npm run import; benchmarks (drop suggested_tasks, assign tasks in data/tasks.json) and ledger (strip action/evidence_url/scope; apply add_match) by hand. Simulated with lib/score.ts toCells: 28 thin models reach >=3 counted results, 35 gain. Validated with scripts/check.ts --validate-only on a merged scratch copy.

benchmarks.name: MT-Bench (GPT-4 single-answer grading, LMSYS runs)
benchmarks.metric: mean GPT-4 single-answer grade (1-10) over the 80 MT-Bench questions, both turns
benchmarks.description: MT-Bench (Zheng et al. 2023, arXiv 2306.05685): 80 two-turn open-ended questions in 8 categories (writing, roleplay, reasoning, math, coding, extraction, STEM, humanities); GPT-4 grades each answer 1-10 (single-answer grading, fastchat.llm_judge) and the score is the mean over all 160 turns. Raw judge-score units kept (kind linear, fixed latent_scale 1 = one MT-Bench point), not converted to accuracy. Only rows LMSYS published in its 2023 leaderboard tables (its own fastchat.llm_judge runs) are recorded; later rows whose values equal the makers' own announcements (e.g. Zephyr, Mixtral, Qwen1.5, Mistral 7B Instruct) are left out because LMSYS may have copied them.

benchmarks.name: MM-MT-Bench (Mistral, GPT-4o judge)
benchmarks.metric: mean judge grade (1-10) over the 92 MM-MT-Bench conversations
benchmarks.description: Multimodal MT-Bench (Mistral AI, Pixtral 12B paper Sec. 3; dataset mistralai/MM-MT-Bench, eval split): 92 conversations over charts, tables, PDF pages, diagrams and miscellaneous images (69 single-turn, 23 multi-turn); an independent LLM judge (GPT-4o in the paper's Table 2) grades each response 1-10 against a reference answer for correctness and completeness; score = mean grade. Raw judge units (kind linear, fixed latent_scale 1 = one point), not accuracy.

benchmarks.name: Ai2 Molmo human preference Elo (Sept 2024, 27 VLMs)
benchmarks.metric: Elo rating from Ai2's pairwise human preference study
benchmarks.description: Human preference evaluation run by Ai2 for the Molmo release (Deitke et al., arXiv 2409.17146): ~15k diverse image+text prompts were sent to 27 vision-language models, and ~870 annotators made ~325k pairwise preference judgments; ratings are Elo/Bradley-Terry scores published in the Molmo model cards ('Human Preference Elo Rating'). One fixed study (Sept 2024); not LMArena vision.

benchmarks.name: Ai2 Molmo2 human preference Elo (video/image QA, 2026)
benchmarks.metric: Bradley-Terry Elo from Ai2's pairwise human preference study
benchmarks.description: Human preference study run by Ai2 for the Molmo2 report (arXiv 2601.10611, Sec. 4.1): 450 manually filtered open-ended questions from annotators plus 51 video-captioning queries; two models' outputs are compared pairwise by annotators (over 105K ratings, 501 per model pair, 21 models); Elo via the Bradley-Terry model. Distinct from the Sept 2024 Molmo study and from LMArena.

benchmarks.name: Molmo2-CapTest dense video captioning F1
benchmarks.metric: statement-level F1 (LLM judge) vs human captions
benchmarks.description: Molmo2-CapTest (Ai2, arXiv 2601.10611): 693 Creative Commons videos, each with at least four human-written captions; an LLM judge scores the precision and recall of statements in the model's caption against the annotators' statements, reported as F1 (0-1).

benchmarks.name: Molmo2-VideoCount accuracy (val)
benchmarks.description: Molmo2-VideoCount (Ai2, arXiv 2601.10611): 533 diverse video counting questions (objects, actions, animals; up to 60 instances) built with the Molmo2-VideoPoint pipeline; accuracy = exact-count match on the val split.

benchmarks.name: HumanEvalExplain (HumanEvalPack, 6-language average)
benchmarks.description: HumanEvalPack explanation task (Muennighoff et al. 2023): the model explains a reference solution in natural language, then regenerates the code from its own explanation alone; pass@1 of the regenerated code, averaged over Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust as printed by the source; greedy. Distinct from HumanEvalSynthesize and HumanEvalFix.

benchmarks.name: HumanEvalFix (HumanEvalPack, 6-language average)
benchmarks.description: HumanEvalPack bug-fixing task (Muennighoff et al. 2023): the model repairs a subtly buggy solution given failing unit tests; pass@1 averaged over Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust as printed by the source; greedy. Distinct from HumanEvalSynthesize and HumanEvalExplain.
